messages.subject: Re: Cluster robust SEs
parts:
Thanks Yves,

 

This is a good source for single equation observed variable models.

 

If anyone is interested where the equations for cluster robust SE s come from, I explain them here:

 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XsyUzaZHs5o&t=396s&pp=ygUOY2x1c3RlciByb2J1c3Q%3D

 

What I do not understand is how this applies to multiple equations with latent variables. Shui Fan shared your slideset that contained the MLR equation on slide 6 (https://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/utrecht2010.pdf).

(∆′W ∆)−1(∆′W ΓW ∆)(∆′W ∆)−1

I can see the analogy with cluster robust SEs for the single equation and observed residuals case. But it is not 100% clear to me how one would get from the single equation case to this equation.

 

Best regards,

 

Mikko

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Cluster robust SEs
parts:
On 7/4/23 12:47, Rönkkö, Mikko wrote:
> This is a good source for single equation observed variable models.

For me, it was useful to see how they go from standard (not-clustered)
sandwich-type robust standard errors to cluster-robust standard errors.

> (∆′W ∆)−1(∆′W ΓW ∆)(∆′W ∆)−1
>
> I can see the analogy with cluster robust SEs for the single equation
> and observed residuals case. But it is not 100% clear to me how one
> would get from the single equation case to this equation.

This one is not specific for cluster-robust standard errors, but could
be used for any type of 'robust' standard errors.

Some useful sources for this particular formula are:

Browne, M. W. (1984). Asymptotically distribution‐free methods for the
analysis of covariance structures. British journal of mathematical and
statistical psychology, 37(1), 62-83. (see page 67).

Shapiro, A. (1983). Asymptotic distribution theory in the analysis of
covariance structures. South African Statistical Journal, 17(1), 33-81.

see also

Shapiro, A. (1986). Asymptotic theory of overparameterized structural
models. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 81(393), 142-149.

Bentler, P. M., & Dijkstra, T. (1985). Efficient estimation via
linearization in structural models. In P. Kirshnaiah(Ed.), Multivariate
analysis VI (pp. 9--42), Amsterdam: North-Holland

and also (showing the connections between various flavors:)

Savalei, V., & Rosseel, Y. (2022). Computational options for standard
errors and test statistics with incomplete normal and nonnormal data in
SEM. Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 29(2),
163-181.
https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10705511.2021.1877548

Yves.

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: Cluster robust SEs
parts:
Hi,

 

Thanks. I did a bit of reading on this and got it now. I found this paper to be the most useful:

 

Savalei, V. (2014). Understanding robust corrections in structural equation modeling. Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 21(1), 149–160. https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2013.824793

 

I wonder, though, if there are any textbooks that explain the various SEs? There are a number of econometrics books that explain robust SEs for observed variable models.

 

Angrist, J., & Pischke, J.-S. (2009). Mostly harmless econometrics: An empiricist’s companion.

 

Wooldridge, J. M. (2010). Econometric analysis of cross section and panel data (2nd ed.). MIT Press.

 

But I have not seen a SEM book that would explain the SEs beyond stating that they exist (e.g. Kline says that there are robust SEs and cites Savalei 2014).

 

Mikko
